summary: Gives IANA directions for managing a registry of special-purpose IPv6 address assignments. This memo is informational. It was replaced by RFC 6890.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4773 directs IANA to create a registry of special-purpose IPv6 address designations. The registry records what each prefix is for and how it is intended to be routed.

subtitle: Directions to IANA for managing the Special Purpose IPv6 address registry.

tldr.problem: IANA needed direction for recording special-purpose designations from its assigned IPv6 address pool.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC directs IANA to maintain a registry recording each designation's prefix, purpose, source RFC, dates, contact where appropriate, and intended routing scope.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4773 is Informational and was obsoleted by RFC 6890.

today: RFC 4773 was obsoleted by RFC 6890, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: The Special-Purpose Address Pool
sections.content: RFC 2928 assigned IPv6 address space to IANA for testing and experimental use. RFC 4773 directs IANA to designate special-purpose address blocks from its assigned pool and to open a registry for managing those designations. Other special-purpose cases are documented in IESG-reviewed RFCs.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA has an IPv6 address pool for special designations, including testing and experiments. This RFC directs IANA to keep a registry of those designations.

sections.title: What the Registry Records
sections.content: For each designation, the registry records the address prefix, the RFC requesting it, the date of designation, any end date, the purpose, and the intended routing scope. For experimental unicast assignments, it also identifies the entity and contact details where appropriate. The RFC notes that a registry entry does not guarantee routability in any particular context.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry records the address, its purpose, and its intended routing scope. An entry does not guarantee that the prefix will be routed.

sections.title: Registry and Address Validation
sections.content: The RFC says routing security relies on authenticating claims of unique control over address blocks. It describes the special-purpose registry as an authoritative source of information about the currency and purpose of the designations. It also suggests machine-readable publication and signatures with associated certificates to help applications confirm registry contents.
sections.plainLanguage: A trusted registry can help validate information about special-purpose addresses. The RFC suggests ways to help applications verify that registry data is current and authentic.
